title: Ingredient Decoder
summary: Paste the ingredients list off the back of a product. This names what each substance is, where it comes from, and whether an animal paid for it. Anything it does not hold, it says so.
note: Origin describes where a substance comes from, not whether the finished product was tested on animals — that depends on the brand and the market it sells into. A plant or synthetic origin says nothing about a testing policy.

ingredients.name: Carmine
ingredients.what: A red pigment made from crushed cochineal insects, used in lipsticks, blushes and some foods.
ingredients.note: Roughly 70,000 insects are killed to produce a kilogram of dye.

ingredients.name: Lanolin
ingredients.what: A waxy emollient extracted from sheep's wool, common in lip balms and heavy moisturisers.
ingredients.note: A wool by-product; its supply is tied to the wool industry.

ingredients.name: Beeswax
ingredients.what: Wax secreted by honeybees to build comb, used as a thickener and barrier agent.

ingredients.name: Honey
ingredients.what: Bee-produced humectant used in masks and cleansers.

ingredients.name: Propolis
ingredients.what: Resin collected by bees to seal the hive; used for claimed antibacterial effects.

ingredients.name: Royal Jelly
ingredients.what: Secretion fed to bee larvae, marketed in anti-ageing formulas.

ingredients.name: Collagen
ingredients.what: A structural protein used as a film-former and humectant.
ingredients.note: Cosmetic collagen is usually taken from cattle hide, pig skin or fish. Plant versions do not exist; 'vegetal collagen' is a different molecule.

ingredients.name: Keratin
ingredients.what: Protein used in hair treatments to smooth and strengthen the shaft.
ingredients.note: Typically sourced from wool, horns, hooves or feathers.

ingredients.name: Elastin
ingredients.what: Connective-tissue protein used in firming claims.
ingredients.note: Usually derived from cattle neck ligaments or aorta.

ingredients.name: Silk Protein
ingredients.what: Protein from silkworm cocoons, used for slip in hair and skin products.
ingredients.note: Silkworms are killed in the cocoon during conventional reeling.

ingredients.name: Guanine
ingredients.what: A pearlescent agent used in nail polish, eyeshadow and shimmer.
ingredients.note: Traditionally made from fish scales; synthetic mica-based pearl is now common.

ingredients.name: Squalene
ingredients.what: A light emollient oil. Squalane is its stable, hydrogenated form.
ingredients.note: Historically taken from shark liver; most cosmetic squalane is now made from olive or sugarcane. The label rarely says which.

ingredients.name: Squalane
ingredients.what: Hydrogenated squalene; a common lightweight moisturising oil.
ingredients.note: Plant-derived unless stated otherwise, but shark-derived supply still exists.

ingredients.name: Stearic Acid
ingredients.what: A fatty acid used to thicken creams and harden soap bars.
ingredients.note: Can come from animal tallow or from palm and other vegetable oils.

ingredients.name: Glycerin
ingredients.what: The most widely used humectant in skincare; draws water into the skin.
ingredients.note: Sourced from animal fat, vegetable oil or synthesis. Labels almost never distinguish.

ingredients.name: Tallow
ingredients.what: Rendered cattle or sheep fat, used in soaps and some creams.
ingredients.note: A slaughter by-product.

ingredients.name: Gelatin
ingredients.what: Protein from boiled skin, bone and connective tissue; used as a thickener and in capsules.

ingredients.name: Shellac
ingredients.what: Resin secreted by the lac insect, used in nail products and hair sprays.
ingredients.note: Insects are commonly harvested along with the resin.

ingredients.name: Ambergris
ingredients.what: A sperm-whale intestinal secretion used historically as a perfume fixative.
ingredients.note: Trade is restricted in several countries; most modern 'amber' notes are synthetic.

ingredients.name: Musk
ingredients.what: Base note in perfumery, now almost entirely synthetic.
ingredients.note: Natural musk came from the glands of musk deer. Several synthetic musks are persistent in water systems.

ingredients.name: Chitosan
ingredients.what: Film-forming polymer used in hair styling and some sunscreens.
ingredients.note: Made from crustacean shells.

ingredients.name: Placental Protein
ingredients.what: Extract used in anti-ageing and hair products.
ingredients.note: Usually taken from sheep or cattle placenta.

ingredients.name: Allantoin
ingredients.what: A soothing, keratolytic agent used in sensitive-skin formulas.
ingredients.note: Originally isolated from cow urine; the cosmetic grade is now generally synthetic or from comfrey root.

ingredients.name: Hyaluronic Acid
ingredients.what: A humectant that binds many times its weight in water.
ingredients.note: Once extracted from rooster combs; the standard supply is now bacterial fermentation.

ingredients.name: Cetyl Alcohol
ingredients.what: A fatty alcohol that thickens and stabilises emulsions. Not drying like ethanol.
ingredients.note: Historically from sperm whale oil; now made from coconut, palm or petroleum.

ingredients.name: Oleic Acid
ingredients.what: A fatty acid emollient and emulsifier.
ingredients.note: Tallow- or plant-derived.

ingredients.name: Beta-Carotene
ingredients.what: Orange pigment and antioxidant.
ingredients.note: Usually from algae, carrots or synthesis.

ingredients.name: Dimethicone
ingredients.what: A silicone that gives products their slip and leaves a smoothing film.
ingredients.note: Some cyclic silicones face EU restrictions in rinse-off products for persistence in the environment.

ingredients.name: Parfum
ingredients.what: A legally protected blend that may contain dozens to hundreds of undisclosed substances.
ingredients.note: Only 26 known allergens must be named separately in the EU and UK. The rest of the formula stays trade secret.

ingredients.name: Phenoxyethanol
ingredients.what: A broad-spectrum preservative, capped at 1% in the EU and UK.

ingredients.name: Parabens
ingredients.what: Preservatives that prevent mould and bacterial growth.
ingredients.note: Five parabens are banned in EU and UK cosmetics; the remaining ones are permitted within concentration limits.

ingredients.name: Sodium Lauryl Sulfate
ingredients.what: A foaming detergent used in shampoos, cleansers and toothpaste.
ingredients.note: An irritant at high concentration rather than a proven toxin.

ingredients.name: Formaldehyde Releasers
ingredients.what: Preservatives that work by slowly releasing small amounts of formaldehyde.
ingredients.note: Free formaldehyde is banned in EU and UK cosmetics; releasers are restricted and must be labelled when they exceed a set threshold.

ingredients.name: Retinol
ingredients.what: A vitamin A derivative that increases cell turnover.
ingredients.note: The EU restricts retinol concentrations in face and body products. Not advised in pregnancy.

ingredients.name: Niacinamide
ingredients.what: Regulates oil, supports the barrier and reduces uneven tone.

ingredients.name: Salicylic Acid
ingredients.what: An oil-soluble exfoliant that clears pores.
ingredients.note: Derived from willow bark or, more usually, synthesised.

ingredients.name: Glycolic Acid
ingredients.what: Water-soluble exfoliants that loosen dead surface cells.
ingredients.note: Lactic acid can be fermented from plant sugars or produced from dairy.

ingredients.name: Titanium Dioxide
ingredients.what: A white pigment and mineral UV filter.
ingredients.note: Banned as a food additive in the EU; still permitted in cosmetics, with restrictions on inhalable powder forms.

ingredients.name: Zinc Oxide
ingredients.what: A broad-spectrum mineral UV filter and soothing agent.

ingredients.name: Mica
ingredients.what: A mineral that gives shimmer to powders, highlighters and polish.
ingredients.note: Child labour has been documented in mica mining in India and Madagascar. Synthetic fluorphlogopite is the alternative.

ingredients.name: Talc
ingredients.what: A soft mineral used to absorb oil and add slip in powders.
ingredients.note: Deposits can occur near asbestos; cosmetic talc must be asbestos-free and is subject to purity testing.

ingredients.name: Kaolin
ingredients.what: An absorbent clay used in masks and pressed powders.

ingredients.name: Iron Oxides
ingredients.what: Red, yellow and black pigments used in foundations and shadows.
ingredients.note: Cosmetic grades are synthesised for purity.

ingredients.name: Palm Oil
ingredients.what: A cheap, stable oil and the base for hundreds of derivative ingredients.
ingredients.note: A leading driver of deforestation and orangutan habitat loss in Indonesia and Malaysia. It hides behind dozens of derivative names.

ingredients.name: Shea Butter
ingredients.what: A rich occlusive fat pressed from shea nuts.

ingredients.name: Jojoba Oil
ingredients.what: A liquid wax close in structure to human sebum.

ingredients.name: Aloe Vera
ingredients.what: Hydrating leaf gel used in after-sun and soothing formulas.

ingredients.name: Argan Oil
ingredients.what: A fatty-acid-rich oil used on hair and skin.

ingredients.name: Candelilla Wax
ingredients.what: A plant wax used where beeswax would otherwise be.

ingredients.name: Carnauba Wax
ingredients.what: A hard palm wax used to structure lipsticks and mascaras.

ingredients.name: Tocopherol
ingredients.what: An antioxidant that also slows oils from going rancid.
ingredients.note: Usually from soy or sunflower; synthetic grades exist.

ingredients.name: Lecithin
ingredients.what: An emulsifier that holds oil and water together.
ingredients.note: Soy is standard; egg-yolk lecithin is used in some formulas.

ingredients.name: Aqua
ingredients.what: Water. Usually the first and largest ingredient in anything that pours.
